# Tobit Chapter 8 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, Tobit 8 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/TOB_008_page_001.jpg

---

**8:1** And when they had finished eating, they brought Tobias in to her.

**8:2** And as he went, he remembered the words-of Raphael, and he took the ashes-of the incense and put upon them the heart and the liver-of the fish, and he made-smoke [with them].

**8:3** And the demon smelled [it] and fled to the upper-parts-of Egypt, and Raphael went and bound him there, shackled-forever.

**8:4** And when they were shut-in together, Tobias rose from the bed and said, "Rise, sister, and let us pray that the-Lord will have-mercy upon us."

**8:5** And Tobias began and said, "Blessed [are] you, O God-of our-fathers, and blessed [is] your name into all the ages-of the ages; let the-heavens bless you, and all your creation into all the ages.

**8:6** You made Adam and gave to-him Eve his-wife [as] a-helper and support; from both-of-them came the seed-of mankind. You yourself said, 'It is not good [for] the man to be alone; let us make for-him a-helper like him.'

**8:7** And now, O Lord, it is not on-account-of lust [that] I am taking this my-sister, but on-account-of truth. Command that mercy be shown to-me and to-her, and that we reach old-age together."

**8:8** And they both said together, "Amen, amen."

**8:9** And they slept for the night. And Raguel arose and went and dug a grave,

**8:10** saying, "Perhaps he also will die." And Raguel went into his house

**8:11** and said to Edna his-wife, "Send one-of the maidservants and let her see whether he is alive; and if not, let us bury him, that no-one may know [about it]."

**8:12** And the maidservant opened the door and went in and found them both sleeping.

**8:13** And the maidservant came out and told them that he was alive.

**8:14** And Raguel blessed God, saying, "Blessed [are] you, O God, with every pure and holy blessing; and let your holy ones bless you, and all your creatures, and all your angels, and your chosen-ones bless you forever.

**8:15** Blessed [are] you, because you made-glad [me], and it has not happened to-me as I feared, but you have dealt with us according-to your great mercy.

**8:16** Blessed [are] you, because you showed-mercy to two only-children. Show them-mercy, O Master, grant to-them health in life and joy, and mercy and cheerfulness.

**8:17** Grant to-them, O Lord, long life in gladness."

**8:18** Then he commanded his servants to fill the grave before it became day.

**8:19** And he told his-wife to bake many loaves, and he himself went to the herd and brought two oxen and four rams, and commanded to-them [them to] prepare [them]; and they began to prepare.

**8:20** Then he called Tobias and swore to-him, saying, "You shall not depart from here for fourteen days,

**8:21** but shall remain here eating and drinking with me, and you shall make-glad the soul-of my daughter who has been afflicted greatly. And take from me immediately half-of what I possess, and go in-peace to your father; the other half [will be yours] when my-wife and I die. Take-heart, child; I am your father and Edna [is] your mother, and we are yours and your sister's now and forever. Take-heart, child."

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

The Sinaiticus (GII) text of chapter 8 is notably longer than the shorter recension (GI/Vulgate). Key observations:

- **8:2-3**: The burning of the fish heart and liver — EMET preserves the precise sequence: ashes of incense, then heart, then liver. The demon's flight "to the upper parts of Egypt" is GII's distinctive expansion; the Vulgate says only "into the remotest parts of Egypt."
- **8:4**: "Rise, sister" — adelphe is literal address, a term of intimacy not implying blood kinship here.
- **8:5-7**: The prayer of Tobias is one of the most theologically rich passages in Tobit. The allusion to Gen 2:18 ("not good for the man to be alone") is explicit. "On account of truth" (ep' aletheias) versus "on account of lust" (ep' porneia) — EMET preserves both Greek terms transparently.
- **8:9**: Raguel "dug a grave" — this darkly ironic detail is unique to the longer recension.
- **8:19**: The feast preparations (two oxen, four rams) reflect the scale of a proper wedding banquet.
- **8:21**: "Half of what I possess" — EMET preserves the legal/commercial texture of this inheritance promise.

*— EMET*
